rule_audit.name: Notice for tenant breach materially affecting health and safety
rule_audit.label: Notice for tenant breach materially affecting health and safety (R.C. 5321.11)
rule_audit.summary: For covered R.C. 5321.05 breaches materially affecting health and safety, the written notice must specify the noncompliant act or omission and a termination date at least thirty days after receipt; timely remedy prevents termination.
rule_audit.excerpt: IN THE FRANKLIN COUNTY MUNICIPAL COURT MEMORANDUM SUPPORTING TERMINATION UNDER R.C. 5321.11 STATEMENT OF FACTS Morgan Taylor rents a residential apartment from Oak Street Homes. Taylor stored open gasoline cans in the only interior exit corridor. The cans obstructed egress and created an immediate fire hazard. On January 1, 2026, Oak Street Homes delivered a written notice t

elements.label: Alleged R.C. 5321.05 breach materially affects health and safety
elements.requirement: Identify the covered obligation and material health-or-safety effect.
elements.explanation: The brief alleges that storing open gasoline cans in the only interior exit corridor breached the tenant's R.C. 5321.05 safety obligation and materially affected health and safety through fire and egress hazards. The declaration corroborates the obstructed exit corridor and immediate fire and egress hazard.
elements.quote: Taylor's storage of open gasoline cans in the only exit corridor breached the tenant's obligation under R.C. 5321.05 and materially affected health and safety.

elements.label: Landlord delivered written notice
elements.requirement: Identify delivery and receipt of a written notice.
elements.explanation: The brief alleges delivery of a written notice on January 1, 2026, and receipt that day. The property manager's declaration states that the notice was hand-delivered and that Taylor signed a receipt.
elements.quote: On January 1, 2026, Oak Street Homes delivered a written notice to Taylor, who received it that day.

elements.label: Notice specified the noncompliant act or omission
elements.requirement: Quote or attach the notice's factual specification.
elements.explanation: The brief quotes the notice's factual specification of the noncompliant conduct. The declaration reproduces the same notice language.
elements.quote: The notice stated: "Remove the open gasoline cans from the only interior exit corridor. Their storage there violates the tenant's safety obligation under R.C. 5321.05."

elements.label: Notice set a termination date at least thirty days after receipt
elements.requirement: Provide receipt and termination dates.
elements.explanation: The brief provides both the January 1, 2026 receipt date and the February 15, 2026 termination date, and alleges the forty-five-day interval. The declaration supports both dates.
elements.quote: The written notice set February 15, 2026 as the termination date, forty-five days after Taylor received it.

elements.label: Condition remained unremedied
elements.requirement: Address remedy within the statutory period.
elements.explanation: The brief alleges that Taylor did not remedy the condition during the statutory period and that the gasoline cans remained after the termination date. The declaration supports that the same cans were observed in the same location on February 16, 2026.
elements.quote: Taylor did not remedy the condition during the statutory period; the cans remained in the corridor when the property was inspected on February 16, after the termination date.

rule_audit.name: Notice to leave the premises
rule_audit.label: Notice to leave the premises (R.C. 1923.04)
rule_audit.summary: A forcible entry and detainer action requires that the party seeking possession first serve a notice to leave the premises, in the statutory form and by a permitted method, and then wait the statutory period before filing.
rule_audit.source: R.C. 1923.04; Iskin, Ohio Eviction and Landlord-Tenant Law (6th ed. 2022), § I.C

rule_audit.name: Waiver of notice to vacate by acceptance of future rent
rule_audit.citation: Associated Estates Corp. v. Bartell, 24 Ohio App.3d 6 (8th Dist. 1985)
rule_audit.label: Waiver of notice to vacate by acceptance of future rent (Associated Estates Corp. v. Bartell, 24 Ohio App.3d 6 (8th Dist. 1985))
rule_audit.summary: Acceptance after an R.C. 1923.04 notice of rent attributable to a future occupancy period waives that notice; acceptance of only past-due rent does not.
rule_audit.source: Iskin, Ohio Eviction and Landlord-Tenant Law (6th ed. 2022), § II.C.1; Associated Estates Corp. v. Bartell, 24 Ohio App.3d 6, 492 N.E.2d 841 (8th Dist. 1985)
rule_audit.excerpt: nuary 3, 2026. On February 1, Maple accepted Lee's $900 payment and issued a written receipt. Maple nevertheless filed this possession action on the January 3 notice. ARGUMENT Lee expressly invokes Associated Estates Corp. v. Bartell, 24 Ohio App.3d 6 (8th Dist. 1985), and asks the Court to dismiss the possession claim because Maple waived the notice. The landlord served the R.C. 1923.04 notice on January 3. It then accepted Lee's $900 payment on February 1, after service of that notice. The

elements.label: R.C. 1923.04 notice was served
elements.requirement: Identify the notice and its service date.
elements.explanation: This is an unconditional requirement of the invoked waiver rule. The brief identifies the R.C. 1923.04 notice and states it was served on January 3, 2026; the stipulated exhibit confirms service on that date.
elements.quote: Maple Apartments served Jordan Lee with an R.C. 1923.04 notice to leave on January 3, 2026.

elements.label: Landlord accepted rent after notice
elements.requirement: Identify payment and acceptance after service.
elements.explanation: This is an unconditional requirement of the invoked waiver rule. The brief alleges Maple accepted Lee's $900 payment on February 1, after the January 3 notice, and the record receipt and deposit support acceptance.
elements.quote: It then accepted Lee's $900 payment on February 1, after service of that notice.

elements.label: Accepted payment covered a future occupancy period
elements.requirement: Show that some accepted rent was attributable to a period after notice rather than only past-due rent.
elements.explanation: This is an unconditional requirement because the asserted waiver depends on rent attributable to a future occupancy period rather than only arrears. The brief states the receipt applied the payment to March 2026, and the stipulated receipt expressly confirms that allocation.
elements.quote: The accepted payment was not limited to arrears: the landlord's receipt expressly applied $900 to March 2026, a future occupancy period after the notice.
